title: Pinned Chats Reconciliation — dev message architecture

items.title: Immutable migration preflight
items.precondition: Execution branch is based on current dev.
steps: Run the three pin migrations in an isolated database.
items.expected: No duplicate/colliding migration is applied; all three tables and required indexes exist.
items.evidence: 2026-08-05: created disposable PostgreSQL database socmed_pinned_chats_accept_20260805, ran all 30 migrations, verified all three pin tables and migration records, then dropped the database.

items.title: Conversation pins are private and stable
items.precondition: Users A and B share two conversations; A has a second browser tab.
steps: A pins one conversation from the inbox menu.
Send activity in pinned and unpinned conversations.
Inspect A’s second tab and B’s inbox.
items.expected: A’s pin stays first after live refresh; unpinned order follows current activity; B’s order does not change.
items.evidence: 2026-08-05 contained runtime: pinning from A's inbox menu succeeded; A's canonical inbox returned isPinned:true while B's pin state stayed independent. After B pinned too, A deleted and B restored the conversation: A returned isPinned:false and B remained isPinned:true.
items.notes: Browser exercised the inbox menu; API responses verified the actor-scoped ordering/state contract.

items.title: Message pin authorization and visibility
items.precondition: A and B share a conversation; nonparticipant C exists.
steps: A pins and unpins a sent message.
Hide the message for A and retry.
items.expected: A and B receive correct shared pin data; repeat operations are safe; C is forbidden; hidden/unsent content is unavailable.
items.evidence: 2026-08-05 contained runtime: B pinned A's sent message and both pin state/activity payloads hydrated correctly; A unpinned via the browser dialog. Nonparticipant C received 403 MESSAGE_FORBIDDEN; A received 404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND after deleting the conversation; a pinned B message was unsent and the thread returned pinnedMessages:[] afterward.
items.notes: Repeat pin/unpin is implemented as idempotent insert/delete and was covered by the UI/API flow.

items.title: Pinned-message UI preserves current thread features
items.precondition: A and B have a themed thread with searchable messages, reactions, and an existing theme log.
steps: Observe both sessions and use search, reaction, edit/unsend, and theme controls.
items.expected: Pin activity appears in timeline and inbox preview; dialog updates live; existing dev thread features remain functional.
items.evidence: 2026-08-05 contained runtime: thread rendered Pin Tester Two pinned a message in the timeline; Conversation options opened the Pinned messages dialog with the shared message and Unpin action. Existing endpoints remained live: edit, heart reaction, nature-forest theme update/log, search, and unsend all returned their canonical success responses.
items.notes: Browser verified the pin surfaces; API regression checks verified the unchanged dev contracts in the reconciled thread.

items.title: Delete clears only the actor’s conversation pin
items.precondition: A pinned the conversation and B retains it.
steps: B sends A a new message.
items.expected: A’s restored conversation is unpinned; B’s thread and pin state remain unchanged.
items.evidence: 2026-08-05 contained runtime: A's delete hid the conversation and removed A's private pin in the same transaction. B's pin remained true; B sent a new message, restoring A's inbox with isPinned:false.
items.notes: Acceptance exposed the missing deletion cleanup; it was fixed in MessageService, typechecked, and rerun before recording this result.

items.title: Typecheck, build, and focused tests
steps: Run relevant automated tests and npm run check:all if available.
items.expected: All execution-caused failures are fixed or documented as an approved waiver.
items.evidence: 2026-08-05: npm run typecheck and npm run build passed. npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high found 0 vulnerabilities. No automated test or check:all script exists in this repository.
